Records the NEWAGE-0.3a, -0.3b, -0.3b' and -0.3b'' detector generations as one continuing experiment (the collaboration's own framing: 'has updated the results since then', arXiv:2301.04779). The 2015 NEWAGE-0.3b' result (Prog. Theor. Exp. Phys. 2015, 043F01; 31.62 live days per arXiv:2005.05157) is not recorded: the paper is not on arXiv and the journal pages were not readable (HTTP 403).
No official NEWAGE website found (searched 2026-10-26); links.website stays null.
Laboratory B of the Kamioka Observatory has no site record of its own; the Mozumi mine (Super-Kamiokande cavern) site is referenced (see the detector placement note).

physics_goals.quote: NEWAGE (NEw generation WIMP search with an Advanced Gaseous tracker Experiment) is a direction-sensitive direct WIMP search experiment using a low-pressure gaseous micro Time Projection Chamber (µ-TPC) for the detection of three-dimensional (3D) tracks of recoil nuclei.
physics_goals.value: Direction-sensitive search for WIMP dark matter with a low-pressure gaseous micro-TPC

summary.plain: NEWAGE is a Japanese dark matter experiment in the Kamioka mine that tries to tell which way a dark matter particle came from. It tracks the recoil of a nucleus in a low-pressure CF4 gas chamber, which could show whether recoils point back along the direction of the Solar System's motion through the Galaxy.
summary.technical: NEw generation WIMP-search with an Advanced Gaseous tracking device Experiment: direction-sensitive WIMP search with low-pressure CF4 micro-TPCs read out by a micro pixel chamber (mu-PIC) with GEM pre-amplification, in Laboratory B of the Kamioka Observatory (2700 m.w.e.). Spin-dependent WIMP-proton limits from direction-sensitive analyses: 5400 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (NEWAGE-0.3a, 0.524 kg d, 2010), 50 pb at 100 GeV/c^2 (NEWAGE-0.3b'', 2021) and 25.7 pb at 150 GeV/c^2 (3.18 kg d, 2023).
